commentary: A 25-year-old strategy game just got the movie treatment it never had — made by **one person with AI**, not a studio

credit.name: @evolving.ai
credit.note: original creator unnamed in the source

caption:
Red Alert 2 — the 2000 RTS — rebuilt as a live-action war film by one person using AI video.

Tanya. Kirov airships. Apocalypse tanks. The exact units, not a loose homage.

This is the part that should worry studios and excite everyone else: a 25-year-old game finally got its movie, and it took one creator instead of a production house.

For context on where the models are: ByteDance shipped Seedance 2.5 on 31 July — 30 seconds in a single generation, up to 50 reference inputs. Seedance 2.0 currently leads the Artificial Analysis video arena ahead of Veo 3.1 and Kling 3.0. I can't confirm which model made this particular film, so I'm not going to claim one.

Clip via @evolving.ai. The original creator isn't named in the source — if you know who made it, tag them and I'll credit properly.

What would you rebuild first?
